# dsh-callout GitHub-style alert cards for [DeepSeek Harness (DSH)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) assistant Markdown. It turns a qualifying `> [!NOTE]` blockquote into a compact, theme-aware card without changing stored session content or DSH's core renderer. ## See it first ```markdown > [!WARNING] > This operation may overwrite existing configuration. ``` Install the plugin, refresh DSH Web, then send that assistant Markdown. A qualifying leading marker becomes a warning card; malformed or unknown markers remain ordinary text. ## Why this plugin exists A warning should look like a warning before the reader reaches the command. A key decision should be easy to find without wrapping the entire answer in a colored box. `dsh-callout` keeps the source format readable Markdown and upgrades it only at presentation time: ```text assistant Markdown → DSH MarkdownText → ordinary blockquote → callout card ``` It does not modify stored session content, providers, permissions, tools, or the DSH core renderer. ## Supported types | Type | Use it for | Accent | |---|---|---| | `NOTE` | Premises, environment facts, and boundaries | Blue | | `TIP` | A better or less obvious approach | Green | | `IMPORTANT` | A decision or key conclusion | Purple | | `WARNING` | Potential loss or destructive operations | Amber | | `CAUTION` | High-impact or difficult-to-reverse operations | Red | ## Visual map The two diagrams below keep the proof close to the implementation: the type palette shows the supported semantic cards, and the flow shows the guarded DOM upgrade path.

## Install No settings. After install, the host half injects the authoring contract into the system prompt, and the browser half upgrades qualifying assistant Markdown. ### From GitHub ```powershell dsh plugin --profile web add github:Aafff623/dsh-callout ``` Then hard-refresh the Web UI (`Ctrl+Shift+R`). `dsh.bundle.patch` inserts the plugin into the profile bundle. `lib/` is committed, so a git install needs no local build. ### npm Not published yet. `dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-callout` works only after the package is on the registry you use. ## Canonical syntax Use one of these two forms: ```markdown > [!NOTE] > Body text on the next line. ``` ```markdown > [!NOTE] Body text on the same line. ``` The marker must be the first content of the blockquote. Every physical line in a multiline callout starts with `>`. These are not canonical callouts: ```text [!NOTE] Body without the `>` marker. ``` ```text Intro text > [!NOTE] > body squeezed onto one line. ``` Malformed or unknown markers fail open as ordinary text. The plugin does not attempt to turn every occurrence of `[!NOTE]` into a card. ## What is guaranteed - Five fixed types, case-insensitive. - Code, inline code, emphasis, links, lists, nested quotes, and later paragraphs do not activate the blockquote transform. - The marker is removed only from a qualifying leading text node; the body node is retained. - The observer-echo path is idempotent: the plugin's own text mutation is not mistaken for an edit. - Real edits can remove plugin-owned card chrome and restore the source marker when it is still safe to do so. - Light/dark palette rules follow DSH's `body[data-ds-dark-theme]` switch. ## What this plugin does not do - Human messages are rendered by DSH as plain text and are intentionally outside this plugin's scope. - It is not a Markdown parser replacement and does not add new Markdown AST node types. - It does not guarantee source-level distinction between a real marker and a backslash-escaped marker after Markdown parsing. - The plugin uses the current DSH Web DOM contract; a future renderer change should be checked with the regression suite and a browser smoke test. ## Architecture | Layer | File | Responsibility | |---|---|---| | Host | `src/index.ts` | Injects the concise output contract into the system prompt | | Bundle | `cordis.patch.yml` | Registers the plugin entry in the DSH bundle | | Browser | `src/client/index.ts` | Matches rendered DOM, applies card attributes/CSS, observes streaming updates, and owns teardown | | Verification | `test/callout.test.mjs` | Tests GFM shapes, negative cases, and the observer state machine | Both halves build into `lib/` with esbuild. The browser half is deliberately presentation-only. It uses plugin-owned `data-md-alert-*` attributes and `--dsh-callout-*` variables, and registers cleanup with Cordis `ctx.effect()`. ## Development ```powershell npm install npm run typecheck # tsc --noEmit npm run build # esbuild → lib/index.js + lib/client.js (ModuleLoader-wrapped) npm test # node:test, vm-isolated suite against the built bundle ``` `lib/` is committed on purpose: a git install works with zero build step. If you change `src/`, run `npm run build` and commit the refreshed `lib/` together — CI fails on drift. The test suite currently covers 30 cases, including: - standard one-line and multiline forms; - all five types, lowercase types, CRLF, and CJK text; - unknown/glued markers, code, emphasis, links, lists, nested quotes, and indented/fenced code; - bare assistant-Markdown paragraph fallback; - first upgrade, observer echo, real-edit cleanup, and node-removal release; - incremental dirty-root hits, unrelated mutations that must not clear a card, and a rebuilt parent paragraph. For a quick visual check, open [`demo-before-after.html`](./demo-before-after.html). The diagrams in this README are deterministic implementation maps, not screenshots of a running session. ## Compatibility and maintenance | Plugin | DSH baseline | Status | |---|---|---| | `0.2.x` | `0.1.2-rc.1` | Tested | After a DSH upgrade, run `npm test`, then smoke-test one standard callout, one code example, one theme switch, and one session switch. If the renderer, Markdown root class, client loader, or chat-flow attributes change, review `src/client/index.ts` before upgrading the plugin version. ## License MIT — see [`LICENSE`](./LICENSE). TYPE is one of: NOTE, TIP, IMPORTANT, WARNING, CAUTION (case-insensitive). The plugin also has a narrow compatibility fallback for an isolated bare marker paragraph inside assistant Markdown, but do not rely on that fallback. **The two canonical forms:** \`\`\`markdown > [!NOTE] > Body text on the next line. \`\`\` \`\`\`markdown > [!NOTE] Body text on the same line. \`\`\` **Never do these as canonical output** (they may stay literal; the isolated bare-marker fallback is only a narrow compatibility path): \`\`\`text [!NOTE] Body without the ">" marker — not a callout. \`\`\` \`\`\`text Intro text > [!NOTE] > body squeezed onto one line — not a callout. \`\`\` Rules for the marker itself: - \`[!TYPE]\` must be the first content of the blockquote; no text before it on the first line. - Every line of the callout starts with \`>\`. - Use one TYPE word: \`[!TIP]\`, \`[!NOTE]\`, \`[!IMPORTANT]\`, \`[!WARNING]\`, \`[!CAUTION]\`. **When to use (authoring guidance — the renderer does not enforce counts):** - Key conclusion or a decision the user must make → \`[!IMPORTANT]\` - A better approach than the literal ask → \`[!TIP]\` - A premise, version, or environment assumption → \`[!NOTE]\` - Destructive or irreversible operations (delete, drop, reset, rm -rf, force-merge, …) → \`[!WARNING]\` (potential loss) or \`[!CAUTION]\` (high-risk loss), placed before the command, stating exactly what may be lost. - Pure fact lookup or quick confirmation → skip the callout entirely. **Style guidance:** at most one callout per reply, placed on the key takeaway or the safety note. The body is normal Markdown (plain paragraphs work best; complex structures like tables render but are discouraged).` export function apply(ctx: Context): void { ctx.inject(['systemPrompt'], (injected) => { const { systemPrompt } = injected as PromptContext systemPrompt.section({ name: 'dsh-callout:github-alerts', order: systemPrompt.getSectionOrder('WEB_SURFACE'), text: () => ALERTS_SECTION, }) }) } " }, { "path": "src/client/index.ts", "content": "/** * dsh-callout — browser half. * * Rewrites GFM alerts (`> [!TIP]` …) that the stock DSH markdown renderer * leaves as plain blockquotes into GitHub-style callout cards. * * Contract (keep in sync with src/index.ts and test/callout.test.mjs): * 1. A callout is a Markdown blockquote whose first block is a paragraph * whose first inline child is a plain text node. * 2. That text must start with `[!TYPE]` (NOTE/TIP/IMPORTANT/WARNING/ * CAUTION, case-insensitive) followed by whitespace or end-of-text. * The marker and the body may live in the same text node; only the * marker prefix is removed. * 3. Unknown or malformed markers fail open: the blockquote and its text * are left untouched. * 4. Markers inside code, inline code, emphasis, links, lists, nested * quotes or later paragraphs never activate a callout. * * Safety model: never mutate React-owned element structure. We only * 1. set data-* attributes on the blockquote/p (the renderer never sets * them, so React reconciliation won't fight us), * 2. strip the marker prefix from the leading text node (React while keeping the five GitHub types. const ALERT_RE = /^\s*\[!(NOTE|TIP|IMPORTANT|WARNING|CAUTION)\](?=\s|$)/i // Strip the marker plus at most one following line ending; never touch the body. const ALERT_STRIP_RE = /^\s*\[!(NOTE|TIP|IMPORTANT|WARNING|CAUTION)\][ \t]*(?:\r?\n[ \t]*)?/i const TEXT_NODE = 3 const PLUGIN_SOURCE = 'dsh-callout' // Per-element state: after we strip a marker we record the exact text value // we produced. The mutation observer separately records whether a change was // caused by this plugin or by React/user code, so an observer echo keeps the // card while a real edit clears it. const state = new WeakMap() const ownedElements = new Set() const ownTextMutations = new WeakMap() const ownedTextNodes = new Set() const externallyChanged = new WeakSet() function claim(el: Element, text: string, type: AlertType, kind: AlertKind, prefix: string): void { state.set(el, { text, type, kind, prefix }) ownedElements.add(el) } function release(el: Element): void { state.delete(el) ownedElements.delete(el) externallyChanged.delete(el) } function markOwnTextMutation(node: Node): void { ownTextMutations.set(node, (ownTextMutations.get(node) ?? 0) + 1) ownedTextNodes.add(node) } function consumeOwnTextMutation(node: Node): boolean { const count = ownTextMutations.get(node) ?? 0 if (count === 0) return false if (count === 1) { ownTextMutations.delete(node) ownedTextNodes.delete(node) } else ownTextMutations.set(node, count - 1) return true } function ownerForNode(node: Node | null | undefined): Element | null { let el = node?.nodeType === 1 ? (node as Element) : node?.parentElement ?? null while (el) { if (state.has(el)) return el el = el.parentElement } return null } /** Elements whose subtree must be re-upgraded after the current mutation batch. * The first apply() pass is a full document scan; later passes only walk these. */ const dirtyRoots = new Set() /** Nearest element we should rescan: a blockquote if one wraps the node, else * the nearest paragraph, else the element itself (a newly mounted container). */ function nearestScanRoot(node: Node | null | undefined): Element | null { let el: Element | null = !node ? null : node.nodeType === 1 ? node as Element : node.parentElement if (!el) return null let paragraph: Element | null = null let cursor: Element | null = el while (cursor) { if (cursor.tagName === 'BLOCKQUOTE') return cursor if (cursor.tagName === 'P' && paragraph === null) paragraph = cursor cursor = cursor.parentElement } return paragraph ?? el } function isInsideChatFlow(root: Element): boolean { if (typeof document === 'undefined') return true const flows = document.querySelectorAll('[data-chat-flow]') if (flows.length === 0) return true for (const flow of flows) { if (flow === root || flow.contains?.(root)) return true } return false } function collectDirty(node: Node | null | undefined): void { const root = nearestScanRoot(node) if (!root || !isInsideChatFlow(root)) return // Keep the dirty set minimal: an ancestor scan already covers every // descendant, while a descendant adds no value once its ancestor is queued. for (const queued of dirtyRoots) { if (queued === root || queued.contains?.(root)) return } for (const queued of [...dirtyRoots]) { if (root.contains?.(queued)) dirtyRoots.delete(queued) } dirtyRoots.add(root) } function isAttached(node: Element): boolean { if ('isConnected' in node && (node as Element & { isConnected?: boolean }).isConnected) return true if (node.parentElement) return true if (typeof document !== 'undefined' && typeof document.contains === 'function') return document.contains(node) return false } function releaseRemovedNode(node: Node | null | undefined): void { if (!node || node.nodeType !== 1) return const removed = node as Element // React may report a remove and an add for the same moved subtree in one // observer batch. A node with a new parent is still live; release only // genuinely detached roots. if (isAttached(removed)) return dirtyRoots.delete(removed) for (const dirty of [...dirtyRoots]) { if (removed.contains?.(dirty)) dirtyRoots.delete(dirty) } for (const el of [...ownedElements]) { if (el === removed || removed.contains?.(el)) release(el) } } function handleMutations(records: MutationRecord[]): void { for (const record of records) { if (record.type === 'characterData' && consumeOwnTextMutation(record.target)) { // Own strip: the card is already applied. Do not dirty or treat as an edit. continue } const owner = ownerForNode(record.target) if (record.type === 'attributes' && owner) { // External code removed or altered one of our card attributes. // Re-assert our chrome only when it is actually wrong — our own // no-op writes (same values) must not re-enter as records. if (owner.getAttribute('data-md-alert-source') !== PLUGIN_SOURCE) { const owned = state.get(owner) if (owned) applyAlert(owner, owned.type, owned.kind) } continue } if (owner) externallyChanged.add(owner) collectDirty(record.target) for (const added of record.addedNodes ?? []) collectDirty(added) for (const removed of record.removedNodes ?? []) releaseRemovedNode(removed) } if (dirtyRoots.size === 0) return scheduleScan() } function buildCss(): string { // Icon as a tinted background-image on the title pseudo-element, so the // icon and title share one box and can never drift apart. const iconUri = (t: AlertType, hex: string): string => `url("data:image/svg+xml,${encodeURIComponent( ``, )}")` // The double attribute selector outranks the renderer's own // `.markdown blockquote` rule regardless of injection order. let css = ` [data-md-alert][data-md-alert-source] { box-sizing: border-box; border: 1px solid var(--dsh-callout-border-subtle, rgb(0 0 0 / 12%)); border-left: 4px solid var(--dsh-callout-border, #30363d); border-radius: 8px; padding: 10px 14px; margin: 12px 0; background-color: var(--dsh-callout-bg, transparent); color: inherit; } [data-md-alert][data-md-alert-source]::before { content: attr(data-md-alert-title); display: block; min-height: 16px; box-sizing: border-box; padding-left: 24px; font-size: 13px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: .04em; line-height: 16px; color: var(--dsh-callout-fg, inherit); background-image: var(--dsh-callout-icon); background-repeat: no-repeat; background-position: left center; background-size: 16px 16px; margin-bottom: 6px; } blockquote[data-md-alert] > :first-child { margin-top: 0; } blockquote[data-md-alert] > :last-child { margin-bottom: 0; } ` // GitHub Primer palettes: default = light, overridden under dark scheme. // Variable prefix --dsh-callout-* is plugin-owned; never squat --dsh-*. // Background tints derive from the accent via color-mix so light/dark // stay tied to one source of truth per type. const palette: Record = { note: { lightBd: '#0969da', lightFg: '#0969da', darkBd: '#1f6feb', darkFg: '#58a6ff' }, tip: { lightBd: '#1f883d', lightFg: '#1a7f37', darkBd: '#238636', darkFg: '#3fb950' }, important: { lightBd: '#8250df', lightFg: '#6639ba', darkBd: '#8957e5', darkFg: '#ab7df8' }, warning: { lightBd: '#bf8700', lightFg: '#9a6700', darkBd: '#9e6a03', darkFg: '#d29922' }, caution: { lightBd: '#cf222e', lightFg: '#d1242f', darkBd: '#da3633', darkFg: '#f85149' }, } for (const t of TYPES) { const light = iconUri(t, palette[t].lightFg.replace('#', '')) const dark = iconUri(t, palette[t].darkFg.replace('#', '')) const bd = palette[t].lightBd const dbd = palette[t].darkBd // Dark scoping follows the DSH theme system (body[data-ds-dark-theme]), // NOT prefers-color-scheme: DSH can force dark while the OS is light. css += ` [data-md-alert="${t}"][data-md-alert-source] { --dsh-callout-border: ${bd}; --dsh-callout-fg: ${palette[t].lightFg}; --dsh-callout-icon: ${light}; --dsh-callout-bg: color-mix(in srgb, ${bd} 7%, transparent); --dsh-callout-border-subtle: color-mix(in srgb, ${bd} 22%, transparent); } body[data-ds-dark-theme] [data-md-alert="${t}"][data-md-alert-source] { --dsh-callout-border: ${dbd}; --dsh-callout-fg: ${palette[t].darkFg}; --dsh-callout-icon: ${dark}; --dsh-callout-bg: color-mix(in srgb, ${dbd} 14%, transparent); --dsh-callout-border-subtle: color-mix(in srgb, ${dbd} 26%, transparent); }` } return css } function injectCss(): HTMLStyleElement { const existing = document.getElementById('dsh-callout-css') if (existing) return existing as HTMLStyleElement const style = document.createElement('style') style.id = 'dsh-callout-css' style.textContent = buildCss() document.head.appendChild(style) return style } /** First direct #text child of an element, or null when it starts with a * non-text (code/strong/link/image/…). Only this shape is a real marker. */ function firstDirectTextChild(el: Element): Text | null { const first = el.firstChild return first && first.nodeType === TEXT_NODE ? (first as Text) : null } /** Extract the callout type when `nodeValue` starts with `[!TYPE]`, else null. */ function matchMarker(nodeValue: string): AlertType | null { const m = nodeValue.match(ALERT_RE) return m ? (m[1].toLowerCase() as AlertType) : null } /** Strip the leading marker (and one following line ending).
